chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma’ Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whenever one of you intends to go to his wife, so he should not rush it'.
ai.seo_question: What is the prophetic etiquette regarding intimacy with one's spouse?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic emphasis on foreplay and gradual intimacy, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition that views marital relations as an act of worship requiring mindfulness and affection. It underscores the importance of not rushing the process, thereby fostering emotional and physical connection between spouses.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a Abu Sayyar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever one of you intends to go to his wife, so he should not rush it’.
en.sarwar: 48. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al- Rahman from Misma’ abu Sayyar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
When one of you decides to go to bed with his wife he must not place her in a big rush.’”
